title: WPMS/1799/2020 of SHIVAM MINES AND MINERALS THROUGH ITS PROPRIETOR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1782 of 2020
with
WPMS No. 1701 of 2020
WPMS No. 1769 of 2020
WPMS No. 1770 of 2020
WPMS No. 1772 of 2020
WPMS No. 1799 of 2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. B.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate,
assisted by Mohd. Matloob with Mr. Subhash
Upadhyay, Advocates for the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Deputy Advocate
General for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for
Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam.
Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, Senior Advocate,
assisted by Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, Advocate
for respondent no. 4.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
Since common questions of fact and law
are involved in these writ petitions, therefore
these petitions are clubbed together.
However, for the sake of convenience, facts of
WPMS No. 1782 of 2020 are being
considered.
These writ petitions have been filed by
M/s Shivam Mines and Minerals. The reliefs
sought in WPMS No. 1782 of 2020 are
extracted below:
"(i) Issue writ order or direction in the nature
of certiorari calling for the records and
quashing the impugned rejection
order/cancellation certificate (annexure no 3
to the writ petition) by which the technical
bid of the petitioner had been rejected.
(ii) Issue writ order or direction in the nature
of certiorari calling for the records and
quashing the decision of the respondent no.
2 and 3 (annexure no 4 to the writ petition)
by which the financial bid of the respondent
no. 4 has been accepted treating him to the
highest bidder.
(iii) Issue writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the

respondent no. 2 and 3 to declare the
petitioner as technically qualified and to
declare him highest bidder by opening his
financial bid and to award the contract to
the petitioner, accordingly."
The facts of the case, in brief, are that a
mining lease has been granted by State
Government to Garhwal Mandal Vikas
Nigam, which is a Government Company.
Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam had
invited e-tenders for grant of mining rights to
private individuals/firms.
Petitioner (Shivam Mines and Minerals)
was one of the bidders in respect of different
mining lots in question. Petitioner's technical
bid was rejected on the sole ground that he
has enclosed only one photograph of the sole
proprietor of the firm; whereas, as per the
condition of the tender document, each
bidder was required to enclose two
photographs with the technical bid.
Feeling aggrieved by rejection of his
technical bid, petitioner has approached this
Court challenging the rejection order passed
by Managing Director.
Mr. B.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior
Counsel appearing for the petitioner has
drawn attention of this Court to a judgment
dated 16.10.2020 passed by Division Bench
of this Court in Special Appeal No. 212 of
2020
Learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner relies upon paragraph no. 13 of the
said judgment and submits that identical
dispute between the same parties was
resolved by the said judgment. Paragraph no.
13 of the aforesaid judgment is extracted
below:-
"13. It is further brought to our notice that
certain other bids were also rejected on the
ground of non-furnishing of the photographs
and some on other reasons. Under these
circumstances, we hold that the rejection of the
tender document of the petitioner as well as

anyone else, on the ground of non-furnishing
of the photograph, is unacceptable. The
rejection on this ground for all the bids
concerned is set aside. However, so far as the
rejection of the bid on other reasons are
concerned, we leave it to the discretion of the
concerned authorities to assess the same, to
find out whether it constitutes an essential or
nonessential requirement and thereafter to
proceed further in the matter. It is for the
concerned respondents to determine the
same."
He therefore, submits that the present
writ petitions be decided in terms of the
judgment dated 16.10.2020 rendered in
Special Appeal No. 212 of 2020.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel
appearing for Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam
does not dispute the aforesaid submission
made on behalf of the petitioner and, in fact,
he also submits that the present writ
petitions can be decided in terms of the
judgment rendered by Division Bench in
Special Appeal No. 212 of 2020.
 In view of consensus expressed by
learned counsel for the parties that identical
question of law was decided in Special Appeal
No. 212 of 2020, the present writ petitions
are also disposed of in terms of the judgment
dated 16.10.2020 rendered in the said
Special Appeal. However, respondent no. 4
shall be at liberty to make representation to
the employer regarding grievance, if any, on
or before 06.11.2020. If such representation
is made, the same shall be considered in
accordance with law.
(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
 03.11.2020
Navin
